items.title: Louis James Interview, 1959-05-25
items.q: I probably used to play with the Robichaud

ctx.x: Or Teo, do you remember how he did that?

No, I don't, I don't remember how he did it. But I, I tried to figure out, you know, I had a B in the A clarinet. See, we used to get in and use it too, you know. Yes. Well, I couldn't, I couldn't transpose like, probably used to play with the Robichaud, what is his name again? McCurdy? McCurdy, yeah. He could transpose, you know. He could play an A on his B. But now, for me to play that A music, I'd make C. And the violin player had to tune over again, you know, make A and I'd make C. Then I could play that A…
Oh, I was going to ask, did you ever play in a brass band with your clarinet, like an E flat clarinet or anything?
